shortlist.label: Pituitary macroadenoma

shortlist.label: Meningioma

shortlist.label: Pituitary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large sellar/suprasellar mass with aggressive features, such as bony remodeling and invasion of surrounding structures, consistent with a pituitary carcinoma

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
shortlist.why_kept: Central hypothyroidism and progressive visual disturbance, consistent with lymphocytic hypophysitis, although less likely given the large size of the mass

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a large pituitary macroadenoma, including bitemporal headache, progressive diminution of vision, and a large sellar/suprasellar mass on CT and MRI. The presence of central hypothyroidism also supports this diagnosis, as pituitary macroadenomas can compress the pituitary gland and stalk, leading to hormonal deficiencies.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with calcifications on imaging, which were not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually has a more homogeneous appearance on MRI and may have a dural tail sign, which was not described

rejected.label: Pituitary carcinoma
rejected.why: Rare and typically requires evidence of metastasis or aggressive behavior, which was not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with inflammation and enhancement of the pituitary gland on MRI, which was not described in the case
